correctness.rationale: All finite-chain nilpotent orbits are acyclic paths and a strictly increasing partial map forces every nontrivial orbit to be strictly monotone. Parity bounds orbit length by ceil(n/2). Equality forces a full parity-class path and translation by two on mandatory sources. The fence-adjacency equivalence forces every optional opposite-parity point to share that translation, including end boundaries; no other map can maximize. Odd/even Boolean-family inclusion-exclusion produces both rank polynomials. Independent exhaustive map/iterate checks verified all maps n=3..10, including overlapping even cases, as corroboration only. n=1,2 excluded.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a sharp infinite-family nilpotency bound, a rigidity classification of all maximizers that excludes nonisometric elements despite the ambient monoid admitting them, and exact rank generating polynomials with parity-dependent Boolean-cube intersections. This bridges a concrete gap between known full-monoid enumeration and power-index stratification; it is neither a renamed total count nor a small isolated computational exercise.
